8  F Y 2027 - 2031 | C A P I TA L I M P R O V E M E N T P L A N
FY 2027 - 2031 Capital Improvement Plan
The Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) is prepared each year to serve as a budget and planning tool. It is designed
to assist with identifying the location, timing and funding of infrastructure projects for the next five years.
Projects identified are based on School Board and Superintendent priorities, available funding, current facility
conditions and the needs of the schools to accommodate programs and student populations.

The types of projects included in the CIP are new schools, additions, renovations, major replacements and
other large site improvements. A capital improvement project should have a cost greater than $25,000 and
extends the useful life of the asset by at least one year. The included cost estimates are based on the information
available at the time the CIP is created and are subject to change based on final specifications of each project
and current market conditions.

Manassas City Public Schools (MCPS) CIP is a component unit of the City of Manassas CIP. Since MCPS
cannot issue debt or appropriate funding, the school district follows the rules, regulations and policies of the
City of Manassas. The School Board adopts the CIP in March and the City Council adopts the CIP in May.

Capital Improvement Plan Funding
Projects in the CIP are funded using one of the below funding sources:

Capital Improvement Fund (PAYGO)
The Capital Improvement Fund is funded by current revenue received from the City of Manassas.

Bonds

FY 2027 - 2031 | Capital Improvement Plan
Bonds are a type of security sold to finance capital improvement projects to spread the construction cost of a
facility over time, such that those who benefit from it over time also assist in funding it. For any projects to be
funded with bonds, debt service is included as an operating cost. MCPS cannot issue its own debt so the City
maintains responsibility of bond issuances. All of the City’s debt is general obligation bonds.

Other Sources
Other funding sources may include: the use of proffers/cash in lieu, contributions from other governments,
donations, proceeds from land sales, use of reserves, or use of funds from closed projects.

School Division Facility Assessment and Master Plan
On February 10, 2026, the Manassas City School Board approved a contract for a facility assessment that will
involve a comprehensive, community-engaged process for long-term facilities planning and redistricting options.
This facilities assessment will begin in spring 2026. For redistricting, the assessment will develop a model based
on actual 2025–2026 enrollment to maximize existing facility use; collaborate with School Board members,
administrators, parents, and community stakeholders; analyze projections, demographics, and transportation
efficiencies; facilitate public meetings and feedback processes; and present final boundary recommendations to the
School Board and City Council. In addition, the assessment will provide grade configuration recommendations
for five elementary schools, two intermediate schools, and one middle school, and develop a facilities master
plan covering 2027–2042. This plan will include community-informed priorities, optimal PK–8 facility usage
(including the opening of the new Jennie Dean Elementary School in August 2026), renovation and construction
planning, sustainability and equity considerations, cost estimates or cost-guidance processes, and Facility
Condition Index (FCI) ratings for each school to support future Capital Improvement Plans (CIP).

Enrollment and Capacity
MCPS’s projected enrollment for FY 2027 is 7,298 which is 94 fewer students than FY 2026. Although enrollment
has been trending down over the past few years, enrollment has remained relatively flat and we anticipate an
increase in enrollment as new residential areas under construction are completed over the coming years. Based
on projected enrollment, all buildings will remain under student capacity.
